attack_mechanism: When the instruction decoder selects R4 as `reg_src` or `reg_dest`, the execution unit presents its value to the ALU operand network. An internal probe of `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_out` during a chosen MOV, logical, add, or shift operation reveals R4 directly or as a known reversible function. `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_out` is an operand, result, or status-producing intermediate reached while the intervening RTL assignments are qualified by `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.src_reg_src_sel`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.inst_alu`. The observation bypasses direct protection of R4; even a one-bit flag leaks a predicate that can be accumulated over chosen operations. The pertinent register-transfer chain is `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r4 -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_src -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.op_src -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_short -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_out`.

A register-to-register instruction can select R4 on `reg_src` and write the unchanged or ALU-transformed result into another architectural register. Reading or probing `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r3` after the transfer provides an alternate observation point even if R4 itself is protected. `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r3` stores or forwards that copied value after the destination write edge; the intervening RTL assignments are qualified by `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.src_reg_src_sel`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.inst_alu`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.inst_bw`. The attacker obtains the R4 word, or a reversible transform of it, through a less protected register location. The pertinent register-transfer chain is `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r4 -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_src -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_short -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_dest_val_in -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r3`.

An instruction that uses R4 as a source operand, store datum, or address base transfers its contents from the register file into the memory address/data backbone. Probing `openMSP430.mem_backbone_0.dmem_addr` during that transaction exposes R4 directly for a move/store or reveals a deterministic address/data function of R4. `openMSP430.mem_backbone_0.dmem_addr` carries the resulting address, data word, or bus-selected derivative when the intervening RTL assignments are qualified by `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.src_reg_src_sel`, `openMSP430.mem_backbone_0.ext_dmem_en`. The observation discloses all or part of the confidential R4 value and repeated chosen instructions can resolve otherwise masked bits. The pertinent register-transfer chain is `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r4 -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_src -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.op_src_in_jmp -> openMSP430.mem_backbone_0.eu_dmem_addr -> openMSP430.mem_backbone_0.dmem_addr`.
